findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses an abstract class without implementing its abstract methods
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body (`pass`). StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For any detector with type `metric_alert_fire`, this now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler`. Before this change the handler instantiated fine and returned `[]`. The exception propagates out of `process_detectors` and aborts processing for every detector in the batch. Either keep it a plain `DetectorHandler` with a no-op `evaluate` returning `{}`, or implement all the abstract methods. The `TODO: This will be a stateful detector` comment above the class is also stale or misleading now.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` signature now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the docstring still says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". The new abstract `build_occurrence_and_event_data` also has no docstring explaining the contract: what `value` is, and that the returned event_data must be valid for `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`. Both are needed by subclass implementers.

findings.title: Mock hook ignores `value`, so tests cannot catch wrong arguments being passed to the new hook
findings.body: `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` delegates to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event`, which ignores `value` and builds output only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Several tests pass a hard-coded `6` for the expected occurrence while the real value is 8, 10 or 100 (for example `test_dedupe`, `test_results_on_change`, and `test_state_results_multi_group` with group_2=10). Expected and actual values therefore match whatever the real value is. If `evaluate_group_key_value` passed the wrong value to the hook, no test would fail. A test using a mock or spy that asserts the hook's call arguments would close this gap. There is also no test for the `DetectorPriorityLevel` to `PriorityLevel` conversion beyond HIGH.
